_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS THE HOOKS' OWN GATE IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- sweep \
.githooks/injection-sweep.json
`crates/mnemosyne-cli/tests/git_hooks_smoke.rs` drives the REAL hook files
and the REAL side-workspace lister over throwaway repositories, which is
what makes them injectable at all: the subject is a shell script and the
oracle is a Rust suite. Every injection below removes one distinction those
scripts draw and names the case that must go red for it.
THE FIRST FOUR ARE ABOUT THE SAME DECISION, the one R1078 paid for and
R1127 to R1129 found unread in three gates: exit 1 says THESE SITES BREAK
THE LAW and exit 2 says I COULD NOT READ ENOUGH OF THIS TREE TO HAVE AN
OPINION. The gates answer both. Until R1132 nothing checked that their
callers told the two apart, and one of the four collapses is a tree the gate
never read being COMMITTED.
THE `the-hook-…-reporter` GROUP IS R1136's HALF OF THE CI REPORT — named
rather than counted, because this paragraph said THE LAST FOUR and the
group is neither last nor four (R1297 measured five, sitting in the
middle). The hook used to READ GitHub's answer itself, with three `gh -q`
expressions no test here could execute — measured silent twice, at 14
passed / 0 failed each time, while a real `gh` would have reported a RED
commit as clean. The reading is now `tools/ci-state`, with its own sweep;
what is left to this hook is CARRIAGE, and carriage fails in ways of its
own: asking about the wrong commit, swallowing the answer, passing over a
reporter that could not answer, and reading its REFUSAL as its silence.
THE LAST TWO ARE R1182's ARM, and they are here because the round that added
it did not add them. `check-side-workspaces.sh` grew a THIRD gate under the
same three-code contract, printing the same pair of sentences for exit 1 and
exit 2 — and both arms exit 1, so the sentence is the only thing that tells
them apart. Nothing read either one.
Scoped to the hook suite: nothing here touches a gate's own laws, which
have their own sweeps under tools/.
THE SUITE IS A MODULE OF `all` AND NOT A TARGET. R1171 folded seventy-six of
the cli crate's test files into one binary, this one among them, and a
`--test git_hooks_smoke` after that commit is `error: no test target named`
— which takes the eight injections below with it, since the harness refuses a
sweep whose control reached nothing. Measured on the tree that found it: the
control ran 0 targets. The trailing filter reproduces exactly the population
this command had before the fold.
AND THE FILTER IS NARROWED TO WHAT THE INJECTIONS NAME (R1286). This
manifest does not declare its red sets exhaustive — `red_set` is absent — so
no injection below asserts anything about a case it did not name, and
running the whole `git_hooks_smoke::` suite bought observation nobody claims
on. MEASURED and RE-MEASURED at R1290: 39 cases, of which the injections
below name 8 and the filter carries 9; the other 30 would run twice per
injection, and this is the slowest suite in the repository
because every case spawns cargo inside a throwaway repository. One `--only`
proof was still running after forty minutes.
IT IS SELF-CORRECTING RATHER THAN A LIST TO MAINTAIN. An injection whose
expected red is outside this filter comes back MISSED — the harness calls a
sweep that returns 0 a misaimed injection until something says otherwise —
so a name that falls out of the filter is loud rather than silent.
A manifest that DOES declare `red_set: exhaustive` must keep running its
whole suite; that is what exhaustive means.

injections.name: the-hook-reports-on-whatever-commit-is-checked-out
injections.why: R1136. The reporter is asked about a commit and answers about THAT commit; hand it the working tree's HEAD instead of the published `origin/main` and every sentence it prints is true about the wrong subject — including, on the push that is fixing a red CI, a clean report about the commit being pushed. R1122 paid for this shape one gate over: format perfect, subject wrong

injections.name: the-hook-swallows-what-the-reporter-said
injections.why: the R890 blindness rebuilt one layer up. Four consecutive red runs went unnoticed for eleven hours because nothing here could SEE a red CI; a hook that runs the reporter and drops its output is that same silence, and it is worse, because the gate now looks like it is being run

injections.name: the-hook-passes-over-a-reporter-that-could-not-report
injections.why: the reporter exits 2 only when it could not produce a report AT ALL, and 1 when the commit is red and this push has not named it (R1297); this hook is the one production reader of both. Dropping the status makes a push where nothing was checked, and a push over an unread red, look exactly like a push where CI was checked and found fine — the collapse the first four injections here are about, arriving through a different door

injections.name: the-hook-reads-an-unread-red-as-a-reporter-that-could-not-run
injections.why: R1297. The reporter answers THREE codes and this hook is what turns the middle one into a stopped push. Folding 1 back into the `could not run` arm prints a sentence about the reporter failing over a verdict it produced perfectly — and lets the push go, which is exactly the state that cost two consecutive rounds on 2026-09-02: `is RED`, the failing job, the step that ended it and its annotation, all printed, all behind an exit status that said fine

injections.name: the-reporter-may-rewrite-the-lockfile-it-was-run-with
injections.why: R1115 measured that a cargo command allowed to resolve freely REWRITES a lockfile it disagrees with. A hook that drops `--locked` here edits a tracked file of this repository as a side effect of reporting on CI, and the edit lands in whatever the next commit stages

injections.name: the-lister-reports-an-unreadable-environment-as-one-left-to-the-machine

The environment gate answers 2 for a tree it could not read, and folding that into the finding arm tells somebody a test of theirs leaves a variable to the machine when the gate never got far enough to find one — sending them into a workspace to look for a defect nobody has claimed exists

injections.name: an-unreadable-staged-list-reads-as-an-empty-one
injections.why: R1281 — this is the defect as it stood, a single `|| true` on the line four gates are keyed on. `git diff --cached --name-only` returns non-zero only on ERROR, so that clause masked nothing but a failed read — and a failed read does not look like a failure here, it looks like a repository with nothing staged. Gates 3 to 6 then find nothing to check and the hook exits 0 on a commit no rule was applied to. The same shape as `commit-msg`'s `2>/dev/null`, in the hook that gates every commit

injections.name: a-tree-gate-loses-the-hosted-step-that-took-it
injections.why: R1287 — the census's whole claim is that a compiling gate a hook runs has a hosted twin, and this is what makes the claim refusable: point the hosted `named-environment` step at a different workspace and the `pre-commit` gate it was covering has nothing on any runner. The first injection written for this law aimed at the hosted CLIPPY step and came back MISSED, correctly: clippy had already left the hooks in the same round, so removing its twin cannot orphan anything. An expectation that cannot be reached is a misaimed injection, and the harness said so

injections.name: the-key-stops-telling-two-scopes-apart
injections.why: R1287 — THE HALF NO ORPHAN INJECTION CAN REACH. Dropping the scope from the key only ever LOOSENS the comparison: more commands match, fewer orphans, and the assertion about orphans stays green while the census answers `covered` for gates nothing covers. That is not hypothetical — it is what the first form of this test did to `pre-push`'s workspace clippy, whose apparent twin was `server-features`' one-package clippy over the same manifest, and the answer would have licensed deleting a gate with nothing behind it. So the property is asserted directly, and this edit is what proves that assertion is not scenery

injections.name: a-gate-that-can-only-say-no-verdict-here-is-given-a-job-here
injections.why: R1290 — THE HALF THE LAW ABOVE CANNOT REACH. `every_compiling_gate_a_git_hook_runs_is_one_a_hosted_job_runs` accepts a hosted job as the answer for any hook gate, and never asks whether the job it was given can render a verdict where it was put. This edit puts back the exact step R1290 removed: `unread-declaration` in the `validate` job, which exits 2 — NO VERDICT — on every runner, because the program it holds the declaration against lives under the pushing user's `$HOME`. It was red on `origin/main` for two pushes and the law above stayed green throughout, which is what this injection is the proof of

injections.name: the-four-rs-gates-point-at-the-root-again
injections.why: R1292 — the trigger and the target did not agree. Gates 5c/5d/5f/5g fire when ANY `.rs` is staged and walked the ROOT, while this repository has twenty-six workspace roots; a file staged under `tools/<crate>/` was gated by a tree it is not in, so four whole-workspace walks reported findings about files the commit never touched and none about the file it did. This puts that back: whatever workspace owns the file, the set collapses to the root. It is not hypothetical — R1291 shipped a test under `tools/injection-harness/` that spawns a binary reading `CARGO` without naming it, `named-environment` RAN on that commit over the root, and the hosted job found it one round later. RE-ANCHORED at R1293, which moved the walk into `lib/rs-workspaces.sh` so `pre-push` could ask it too — the SUBJECT outlived the line, and it now reaches five gates across two hooks rather than four in one, which is why its red set grew
